name: Car Inspection Checklist
description: A checklist for inspecting your own car's condition and safety.

items.text: Walk around the car checking for dents, rust, cracks or fresh damage.
Confirm the license plates are present, secure and readable.
Check that doors, hood and trunk open, close and latch securely.
Inspect the windshield and windows for chips or cracks in the line of sight.
Check that mirrors are intact, secure and adjust properly.
Look under the car for fresh fluid leaks or hanging components.
Test both low and high beam headlights for output and aim.
Check brake lights and the center high-mount stop lamp.
items.note: Use a wall reflection or a helper to confirm brake lights at the rear.

items.text: Verify front and rear turn signals and hazard lights flash correctly.
Test reverse lights and the rear license plate light.
Check parking, fog and daytime running lights where fitted.
Confirm no warning lights stay lit on the dashboard after start-up.
Check tire pressure on all tires against the door-jamb sticker.
Measure tread depth and confirm it is above the legal minimum.
Look for uneven wear, cuts, bulges or embedded objects.
Confirm all lug nuts are present and wheel covers are secure.
Inspect the spare tire's pressure and condition.
Verify the TPMS light is off or address the warning.
Test the brake pedal for firm, consistent feel without sinking.
Listen for grinding or squealing when braking.
items.note: Grinding usually means worn pads; have the brakes inspected immediately.

items.text: Confirm the parking brake holds the car on an incline.
Check the steering for excessive play, pulling or vibration.
Verify the ABS and brake warning lights are off.
Listen for clunks over bumps that suggest worn suspension.
Check engine oil level and condition on the dipstick.
Verify coolant level in the reservoir when the engine is cold.
Check brake fluid and power steering fluid levels.
Top up windshield washer fluid.
Inspect belts and hoses for cracks, fraying or leaks.
Check the battery terminals are clean, tight and corrosion-free.
Test the horn for a clear, loud sound.
Check that wipers clear the glass and washers spray properly.
Confirm all seatbelts latch, retract and are undamaged.
Verify the defroster, heater and ventilation work.
Check that warning, oil and fuel gauges read correctly.
Confirm a warning triangle, first-aid kit and required items are aboard.

faq.q: What is a car inspection checklist?
faq.a: It's a step-by-step list for checking your own car's safety and condition — lights, tires, brakes, fluids and wipers — against pass or fail criteria, so owners can catch faults early and prepare for an official inspection.

faq.q: How often should I inspect my car?
faq.a: Do a quick safety walkaround monthly, a fuller inspection before long trips and seasonal changes, and a complete review ahead of any official or emissions inspection. Always investigate a warning light promptly.

faq.q: Does this replace an official vehicle inspection?
faq.a: No. This is a self-inspection to catch issues early. It does not replace a licensed inspection station, your jurisdiction's required tests, or a mechanic's diagnosis of any fault you find.

faq.q: What should I do about a fault I can't assess?
faq.a: Note and, if possible, photograph it, then have a qualified mechanic diagnose it. Do not drive a car with a serious brake, steering, tire or lighting defect until it is repaired.

faq.q: Is this available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the car inspection checklist to walk around the car, or download the PDF to complete on your phone and flag items needing repair.
